title: 6.11.4 Lab: Music, volume and a mute key
description: A tune loops under Star catch, quieter than the effects. The up and down keys step its volume between 0 and 10, and M turns every sound off and on again.

steps.title: A tune under the game
steps.instructions:
The starter is Star catch from 6.11.3, with its chime and thud. It also has `let music;` and `let level = 4;`, the tune's volume as a whole number from 0 to 10. A whole number is easy to show and to step up and down, and `level / 10` turns it into the `0` to `1` that `.volume` uses: 4 becomes 0.4.

In `setup()`, after the two sound effects, load the tune, set its volume, and start it looping:

```js
music = loadSound('/moshion/assets/music.wav');
music.volume = level / 10;   // 4 tenths: under the effects
music.loop();
```

`loop()` plays the tune over and over until `stop()`. It is the one call that waits for the file: asked for before the file has arrived, it is remembered and starts when the file lands, so `setup()` is a fine place for it (6.11.1). Run it. The tune starts once the sketch has had your first click or key, or straight away if your click on Run already counted. The words at the top already said `music: 4 of 10` before you started, because `level` was 4 all along; now the tune really plays at that level.
hints: `music.loop();` goes after the volume line, inside setup().
No tune? Click the game: a browser plays nothing until the player has clicked or pressed a key.

steps.title: Up and down change the volume
hints: Two `if`s, one for `'up'` and one for `'down'`, each with two lines inside.
`level` on its own changes nothing you can hear. `music.volume = level / 10;` is the line that does.

steps.title: M turns everything off
hints: `masterVolume()` with empty brackets reads the level; with a number in them, it sets it.
`music.volume = 0` would mute only the tune and leave the chime and the thud playing. `masterVolume` turns off everything.

requirements.title: The tune loops
requirements.description: A sound's .loop() is called, in setup() or anywhere: loop() keeps one copy going, so calling it again is safe. Help: 6.11.1 (Reading: Sound in a sketch)
requirements.hint: In setup(), after loading the tune and setting its volume: music.loop();

requirements.title: The tune starts quieter than the effects
requirements.description: In setup(), a sound's .volume is set below 1: level / 10, 0.4, or any number under 1. Help: 6.11.1 (Reading: Sound in a sketch)
requirements.hint: music.volume = level / 10; in setup(), before music.loop();

requirements.title: Up and down change the volume
requirements.description: Under kb.presses (one step for each press), one key raises the level (or the volume) and another lowers it, and the volume is set from the level again after each step (a volume line that runs only once, in setup(), does not follow the keys). Any variable name works. Help: 6.3.3 (Reading: moSHion docs: Input edges)
requirements.hint: if (kb.presses('up') && level < 10) { level += 1; music.volume = level / 10; }, and the same for 'down'.

requirements.title: M turns every sound off and on
requirements.description: Under a kb.presses test, masterVolume(...) is set (or a mute variable is flipped), and the code can do both: turn every sound off (masterVolume(0)) and bring it back (masterVolume given something other than 0). Help: 6.11.1 (Reading: Sound in a sketch)
